description_full: Turtle Beach Corporation, an audio and gaming technology company, develops and markets audio and gaming accessory products under the Turtle Beach brand in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, and the Asia Pacific. The company offers headsets, controllers, keyboards, mice, flight and racing simulation hardware, microphones, and fight sticks; accessories, such as mousepads, headset stands and cases, and chargers; and replacement parts for transmitters, headsets, mice, keyboards, controllers, and flight simulation products. Its products are used with video game and entertainment consoles, handheld consoles, personal computers, tablets, and mobile devices. The company serves professional streamers, content creators, and esports gamers; and retailers, distributors, and online customers. Turtle Beach Corporation was founded in 1975 and is headquartered in San Diego, California.

financial_summary: Turtle Beach Corporation is a micro-cap technology business with a $272M market cap on $320M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years and +7% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +106.8pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 16% against a 12% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 35%.

The business throws off $34M in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.25× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.2× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 3.5×.

Management returns a meaningful 7.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 17% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
